prompt: Implement Euclid's greatest-common-divisor algorithm as a RECURSIVE method with base case b == 0. Complete the gcd method, then run the tests.
explanation: Recursive Euclid is a textbook example of shrinking a problem toward a base case: each call replaces (a, b) with (b, a % b), and the remainder strictly decreases until it hits 0. The base case b == 0 returns a, which at that point is the greatest common divisor. Applying Math.abs on entry normalizes negatives once; every deeper call already works with non-negative values because a % b keeps the sign of a.
hints: Write the base case first: if b == 0, the answer is a.
Otherwise return gcd(b, a % b) -- the method calls itself with a smaller second argument.
Normalize negatives by reassigning a = Math.abs(a) and b = Math.abs(b) at the top of the method before anything else.
